[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Core rules:
- Goal each level: reduce all ordinary green pegs to one. A normal green-over-green jump uses two ACTION6 clicks: click a green source (dark halo), then an empty landing exactly two lattice steps away across an adjacent green; source and middle green disappear, landing becomes green. Logical spacing is 48 px. Undo is ACTION7.
- Gray plus = empty regular hole. Green plus = ordinary peg.
- Purple/pink plus = permanent jump post: green or red may jump over it into an empty landing; the purple post remains and does not count toward the final green. A purple post can also ride a yellow movable platform.
- Red plus = leapfrogging movable post. Green can jump over red without removing it. Red can be selected and jump over an adjacent green without removing it. Alternating red-over-green and green-over-red moves both along a line without changing green count.
- Orange/yellow black-backed plus = movable one-hole platform. It can be an empty jump destination and carry green, red, or purple.
- Multiple platforms respond to the same arrow simultaneously; adjacent platforms can advance as a train into cells vacated simultaneously. Blocked platforms stay put. Rail junctions/dead ends separate or synchronize them.
- Levels can exceed the viewport. Camera pans to follow moving platforms or jump animations; track invariant world relationships.
- When no useful green moves remain with >1 green, a retry icon appears. Arrows can still move platforms, but retry is not success.
- Direction arrows move platforms only; they do not execute peg/post jumps.
Known solved patterns:
- L1 basic chain; L2 platform bridge; L3 synchronized platforms/camera; L4 permanent-post routing; L5 carried-purple bridge and long hidden multi-board chain.
- L5 large section: move purple platform around perimeter rails to bridge gaps; ordinary merges can be staged by transporting a survivor beside a static green, then jumping the static green over it.
- L6 red-post routing: alternating red/green leapfrogs traverses long corridors. Load both green and red on the two transport platforms before departure. At later isolated three-hole green branches, carry red on the U-rail platform to bridge gaps; green crosses red and merges through the branch, then reposition the red platform to the next corner.
